channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: The Coalition’s Plan To Kill The Illicit Tobacco Market And Smash The Gangs
item.description: Australia’s illicit tobacco crisis cannot be solved by raids alone. The Coalition’s plan recognises a hard lesson: organised crime thrives where taxes create huge margins, legal alternatives are restricted and consumers are pushed outside regulated channels. Cutting criminal profit must go hand in hand with bringing vapes and nicotine pouches into an accountable adult market. Public health is stronger when enforcement, taxation and harm reduction all point in the same direction. (Published on September 03, 2026byliberal.org.au)

item.title: Arielle Selya: The scientist who challenged the gateway theory
item.description: The gateway theory has shaped nicotine policy for years, often turning vaping into a presumed pathway to smoking rather than a potential route away from it. Challenging that assumption matters because policy should follow observed behaviour, not fears repeated until they sound like evidence. Research that separates correlation from causation can help clarify whether safer nicotine products are driving harm or displacing cigarettes. Public health needs that distinction before it builds restrictions around a theory. (Published on September 03, 2026bysnusforumet.se)
